query: I want to get a standing desk but I'm not sure if I should get a motorized one or a manual crank. Is the price difference worth it?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Wirecutter, USA): Wirecutter recommends the Uplift V2 or Flexispot E7 as top motorized sit-stand desks — smooth electric adjustment encourages more frequent position changes, which is the entire health point of a standing desk.

Source 2 (2022, The Verge, USA): Manual crank desks (IKEA SKARSTA, Flexispot crank models) cost $200–300 versus $500–700 for quality motorized options — the manual crank takes 30–40 seconds to adjust, which most users report makes them change positions significantly less often.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/StandingDesk, Global): Community almost universally recommends motorized over manual — frequent position switching is the health benefit, and users report that the friction of manual cranking causes them to stay in one position for hours.

Source 4 (2022, Consumer Reports, USA): Motorized desks have more potential failure points (motor, controller, keypad) but most quality models carry 5–10 year warranties — the reliability gap over manual desks is minimal for reputable brands.

Source 5 (2021, Occupational and Environmental Medicine, UK): Research confirms that the frequency of sit-stand transitions matters more than total standing time — desks with memory presets that enable one-touch height change produce significantly more transitions than manual alternatives.
atoms: perspective: Budget-constrained buyer willing to accept manual adjustment
perspective: User prioritizing health benefit over cost
plausible_answers: Get a motorized desk, since the $200–400 premium removes crank friction that discourages position changes and defeats the health purpose.
Buy an IKEA SKARSTA manual crank desk if budget is tight, since disciplined users with timers still achieve enough variety.
Get a motorized desk with programmable presets, since one-touch height switching is most associated with frequent transitions and health benefit.
